title: Hands-On With Chanel's High-End Men's J12 Golden Black Ceramic 42mm Watch | aBlogtoWatchHands-On With Chanel's High-End Men's J12 Golden Black Ceramic 42mm Watch | aBlogtoWatch
text: Back in April of 2026, I covered the news that Chanel was (after a long wait) introducing a new set of thoroughly masculine Chanel J12 collection timepieces. I wrote about the two new 42mm matte-black ceramic J12 models prior to physically seeing them, and later I did get a chance to meet with Chanel and go hands-on with not only the two new matte black Chanel J12 Golden Black and SUPERLEGGERA Caliber 12.1 watches, but also at least two other models that are designed for men. Even though Chanel has no men’s focus that I can see in their marketing, it still has a lively pulse when it comes to its men’s watch creation team. That said, many of the new women’s Chanel watches steal the artistic focus — how can you beat an entire capsule collection of timepieces with 8-bit-style pixelated Coco Chanel figurines? In a separate article, I also reviewed the new-for-2026 Tudor Black Bay Ceramic Full Bracelet “All Dark” watch, which I think is a cousin to the Chanel J12. Normally, people don’t talk about Chanel and Tudor products in the same conversation, but the comparison is merited in this instance. First, Chanel’s 12.1 automatic movement, contained in most of its J12 watches, is produced by Kenissi, which is in the same building as Tudor’s factory in Switzerland and in which Chanel has a stake. I visited Kenissi in 2023 when I was there to see where Tudor makes its watches. The Caliber 12.1 movement is based on the same architecture as Tudor’s manufacture movements, and while they aren’t the same, they are rather similar. The Caliber 12.1 automatic operates at 4Hz with 70 hours of power reserve and is a COSC-certified chronometer. Chanel uses a unique style of automatic rotor and finishes the movement differently, but I think it is safe to say that Tudor MT and Chanel Caliber 12.1 movements are very close siblings.Advertising Message The similarities between the Chanel J12 and the Tudor Black Bay Ceramic don’t end there. The high-quality ceramic cases and bracelets feel similarly engineered, and the new Tudor Black Bay Ceramic’s black ceramic bracelet has a very similar architecture to Chanel’s popular three-link J12 ceramic bracelet. I suspect that the same supplier is performing services for both of them, which makes sense since Tudor and Chanel clearly shared business interests in Kenissi. What is interesting is that both brands, for different reasons, offer black ceramic watches to their customers. Nevertheless, I think if you like the Tudor Black Bay Ceramic, you will probably like the Chanel J12 Golden Black (and other matte-finished models), too. While I plan to discuss some of Chanel’s other new watches for 2026 in separate articles, my focus right now is the Chanel reference H11060 J12 Golden Black Caliber 12.1 42mm watch. I was really excited about this watch mainly because I missed the 42mm width of the Chanel J12, and because I wanted to see if, after a number of years, Chanel offered any upgrades or improvements to the platform since it has been around since the early 2000s. The most notable upgrade since Chanel last made larger versions of the J12 is the switch from a Swiss-made ETA movement to the Kenissi Caliber 12.1, as well as the price. In other ways, Chanel has very much left the core J12 platform the same. I don’t think the brand needed to update the design, but it would have been nice to see some new ways of doing things, similar to how Rolex updates watches with new technology while making them look more or less the same. Chanel also doesn’t explain why it is returning to men’s J12 watches or even much about the J12 in general. The website now tells people that the general, larger J12 collection was inspired by the J-class of racing yachts that were used in the original America’s Cup boat races. J-class yachts are, indeed beautiful, but I’m not sure that explains why these watches look the way they do or why they are ceramic. I think the new J12 Golden Black 42mm is beautiful and comfortable, but I feel a bit underwhelmed for the price. Let me explain. Chanel is by no means a cheap brand, but the 38mm wide J12 watches with the Caliber 12.1 movement have a retail price of $8,350. Why then, does the 42mm-wide J12 Golden Black watch have a price that is $3,800 more?Advertising Message Chanel might say that the J12 Golden Black 42mm isn’t just a bit larger, but that it contains some gold. Indeed, there are smaller, 38mm-wide polished ceramic versions of the Golden Black that have an 18k gold bezel and crown. That particular model (the Chanel H9541) costs a whopping $7,650 more than the similar 38mm-wide version in just ceramic with steel accents. This larger H11060 J12 Golden Black has a black-coated steel bezel and no solid gold elements on the case or dial. I don’t know if it is solid gold (I don’t think it is), but the automatic rotor for the J12 Golden Black model is gold-toned, while on most other Caliber 12.1 watches the rotor is silver-toned. The attractive aged gold colors on the watch appear to be mostly coatings, with the exception that the applied Arabic numeral hour markers are “gold-plated.” I understand that gold is expensive these days, but it just feels difficult to digest the fact that some gold coatings, paint, and trace material used to plate some hour markers and indicators are sufficient to command this type of price premium. This is a great watch overall, but Chanel seems to sabotage the ability of these new men’s 42mm wide J12 watches to sell at volume by insisting on such pricing schemes. What I love about the J12 isn’t just that it is a dive-style-looking watch, but that you can also technically dive with it given the 200-meter water-resistance rating for the monobloc-style case. Perhaps less than ironically, the Tudor Black Bay’s ceramic case is also water-resistant to 200 meters. Around the dial is a unidirectional rotating timing bezel with a ceramic insert. While luminant is not a forte of the J12, in other ways, I think it is one of the most beautiful and cosmopolitan diver-style watches in the high-end fashion watch market. As I said above, the case is 42mm wide, and it is 12.5mm thick with an AR-coated sapphire crystal over the dial. There is another sapphire crystal over the back, allowing for a view of the mechanical automatic movement inside. Like other Chanel J12 watches, the black ceramic bracelet closes with a spring-loaded double-folding butterfly-style deployant clasp. These are a legacy feature, but they still work well and are very comfortable to put on and take off the wrist. I would just not use them for the sportiest of activities, but that isn’t exactly what this watch was designed for (despite some of its more durable features, such as the scratch-resistant ceramic case and ability to submerge deep underwater). These days I am also comfortable wearing a smaller, 38mm-wide Chanel J12, but I still love the boldness and presence of the 42mm-wide case. I have one of the older Chanel J12 42mm matte-black ceramic watches, and I love how it wears and feels. In my opinion, the Chanel J12 matte-black ceramic watch for men was at its most competitive when it cost about the same as, or less than, many competitor watches from even more serious sport timepiece brands. That made the J12 a high-quality stealth hit, suitable for fashion and horology lovers. The Chanel J12 still maintains much of that charm in 2026, but it hasn’t kept up with marketing its dream, and the new higher prices no longer make the watch as competitive an option as in years past. The idea of a black ceramic watch on a matching bracelet is as exciting today as it was 25 years ago, around when the J12 was first debuted. Chanel will do well with the J12 Golden Black 42mm if today’s market independently popularizes black ceramic men’s watches again (as I hope they do). Chanel also seems to suggest that this model is a limited edition (because it says “Limited Edition” on the caseback), though there is no mention of how many pieces it plans to make, or any reference to it being a limited edition on the website. I am curious what you think about it, so let me know in the comments below. Price for the reference H11060 Chanel J12 Golden Black Watch Caliber 12.1 42mm is $12,150 USD.
